claims.text: PCC-WFE (Pearson-correlation weighted feature expansion) adds one new feature to the 178 raw EEG features, giving Dataset 2 with 179 features.
On Dataset 2 (PCC-WFE expanded), XGBoost reaches the highest 10-fold accuracy among the four traditional classifiers (XGBoost > RF > DT > SVM).
The SGRU classifier outperforms the plain GRU classifier on Dataset 1 (ACC 97.33 vs 92.76, Se 88.89 vs 78.86, PPV 97.51 vs 96.45).
The SGRU classifier outperforms the plain GRU classifier on Dataset 2 (ACC 97.43 vs 94.19, Se 89.86 vs 81.13, PPV 97.93 vs 96.70).
SGRU on Dataset 2 is the best overall configuration (ACC 97.43%), above SGRU on Dataset 1 (97.33%) and above all traditional classifiers.
The dataset is balanced: 2300 samples in each of the 5 classes (11500 total).
The capsule reproduces the published results: running `run` executes NewData_ML_Kfold.py and the fig_*.py scripts.

findings.evidence: The Epileptic Seizure Recognition dataset contains 500 segments per patient (23 patients, 5 classes x 100 segments each); the code uses plain KFold over all 11500 rows, so segments of the same patient appear in both training and test folds. The capsule does not report any patient identifier or grouped split.
findings.question_for_authors: Were the folds grouped by patient? If not, what accuracy remains with a patient-wise split?

findings.evidence: load_data fits MinMaxScaler(feature_range=(-1,1)) on the full 11500-sample matrix before KFold, so test-fold values influence the scaling of training folds. The PCC-WFE feature is also computed once on all 11500 samples using the labels (pc(X, y_data) over the whole dataset), so the added feature of a test sample is built from label information of the whole dataset. Both are transductive preprocessing steps that the 10-fold CV does not isolate.
findings.question_for_authors: Was the scaler and the PCC-WFE feature recomputed inside each training fold? If not, how large is the effect on the reported accuracies?

findings.evidence: code/run executes only NewData_ML_Kfold.py and fig_*.py; SGRU_GRU_Kfold.py (the SGRU/GRU experiment behind C3-C5) is never called, and results/output contains no SGRU/GRU lines. The SGRU/GRU numbers exist only as hard-coded tuples in fig_6.py (scores=((92.76,78.86,96.45),(97.33,88.89,97.51))) and fig_8.py (scores=((94.19,81.13,96.70),(97.43,89.86,97.93))); no per-fold log, no seed, no trained weights are stored.
findings.question_for_authors: Can you release the SGRU/GRU run logs (per-fold ACC/Se/PPV for both datasets) and the seeds used, so the numbers in Fig. 6 and Fig. 8 can be reproduced?

findings.evidence: Our re-computation of 'ACC XGBoost Dataset 2 (10-fold mean)' gives 0.9313913043478262 (re-computed), but the authors' stored output (bp_work/capsule-6746514/results/output) gives 0.951304347826, which matches the paper (results/output line 'XGboost:': 0.951304347826). The gap comes from our re-run (environment, port to another language, package version or seed), not from the paper; it is not reported as a paper problem. Related claims: C2.
